metaData.originalTitle: 别再写 Spec 了，开始写 Facts——整个 SDD 运动已经过时
metaData.title: Stop Writing Specs, Start Writing Facts — The Entire SDD Movement Is Obsolete
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article critiques the fundamental flaws of Spec-Driven Development (SDD) in the AI era, proposes replacing natural language specs with executable assertions (Facts), and provides a 90-day migration plan.
metaData.summary: Author Jaroslaw Wasowski retracts his previous article advocating for SDD, pointing out the core contradiction: a Spec is a statistical prediction about an LLM, not a verifiable contract. The non-deterministic nature of LLMs, the Intent Gap, and Spec Drift are systemic issues that cannot be fixed with better prose. The article proposes a Facts-first paradigm: Facts are machine-verifiable executable assertions (tests, properties, contracts) that remain unchanged across model upgrades. This concept traces back to a 57-year tradition of formal methods, starting with Hoare triples in 1969. The author honestly identifies three scenarios where SDD still applies (compliance and regulation, cross-team B2B integration, onboarding new hires) and provides a 90-day migration plan (Audit → Shift → Gate), emphasizing starting to write one fact tomorrow.

mainPoints.point: A Spec is a prediction about the model, not a contract with the model.
mainPoints.explanation: Each time an LLM reads prose, it re-samples its interpretation. Even at temperature 0.0, non-deterministic outputs exist, causing specs to be reinterpreted across different model versions, whereas tests (Facts) remain unchanged across model upgrades.

mainPoints.point: A Fact is an executable assertion that does not rely on model interpretation.
mainPoints.explanation: Facts include individual tests, properties, and contracts. They pass or fail at runtime with exit code 0 or non-0, requiring no LLM involvement, making them stable and reliable.

mainPoints.point: SDD still has value in specific scenarios but should not be the default paradigm.
mainPoints.explanation: Scenarios requiring external readers, such as compliance and regulation, cross-team B2B integration, and onboarding new hires, should retain SDD; internal development should migrate to Facts.

mainPoints.point: Facts-first is the AI-era synthesis of 57 years of formal methods.
mainPoints.explanation: From Hoare triples in 1969 to Design by Contract in 1992, QuickCheck in 2000, and Agent Behavioral Contracts in 2026, the idea of executable assertions has a continuous lineage, and the AI era has brought its value to the forefront.

keyQuotes: A unit test written in the Sonnet 3.5 era passed CI across four model versions: 3.7, 4, Opus 4.5+. Meanwhile, a 1500-word spec describing the same endpoint was reinterpreted by each model — four reinterpretations.
A spec is not a contract. It is a prediction about the model. The model changes, so the prediction is never accurate.
PRDs will disappear. Specs are exiting the inner loop. Only facts can survive anywhere.
